correctness.rationale: Away from 2, an odd prime maps to an even composite and a composite to a prime, so an odd cycle must contain 2. If k+2 is composite, the next steps from 2 go through an odd prime and an even composite to a prime at step four; that either returns too early or has an even composite at step five. Otherwise the first three steps end at P+(2(k+1))=q; q=2 returns too early and q>2 gives the last composite k+q. It returns to 2 exactly for a power of two. Conversely q<=k+1<k+2 separates the three primes and also precludes equality of the two even composites. Determinism yields uniqueness. In the divisor parametrization 2^m+1=q+(k+1)=qh, so h>=3 is odd, and P+(q(h-1))=q iff P+(h-1)<=q; reversing gives all hypotheses and positive odd k. The separate direct return-time test from 2 using trial division reproduced exactly (5,3,3), (21,11,5), (51,13,6), (59,5,6), (1365,683,11) for the stated finite range.
residual_risks: The replay is bounded by k<=5000. Unbounded correctness rests on the parity and orbit argument, not the enumeration. No formal certification was performed.
